THE PROBLEM
  • Each local representation is built only from its own quadrant
  • No information crosses a boundary until the next layer
  • So the top-left can never use the bird
All the pooling methods we have seen are local gates. They only use local information.

SiLU → SwiGLU, local → global gating
Remember the activation-functions lecture: we have fixed local only info once already
?
BEFORE THE NEXT CLICK
  • What does each SiLU gate get to see?
  • How did we let the gate see more?
SiLU: gate k reads only ŷₖ
p̂ₖ = ŷₖ · g(ŷₖ)
SwiGLU: gate k reads every ŷ
p̂ = ŷ ⊙ SiLU(ŷWᵀ)
Pooling today: a quadrant's gate reads only its own quadrant
Next: a quadrant's gate reads every quadrant
Same move as SwiGLU: let the gate read everything.
Value projection V not drawn. Full SwiGLU is SiLU(XWᵀ) ⊙ XVᵀ; here the value projection is folded into ŷ = XVᵀ, so the gate reads ŷ through its own W.

SiLU vs SwiGLU, as vectors
Ŷ in, P̂ out. SwiGLU adds one thing: a projection Wᵀ before the gate
The only difference: a projection Wᵀ before the gate, so each gate reads every unit of Ŷ
Attention keeps this pattern: projections feed the gate.

Max pooling is a gated sum: gate 1 on each window’s max, 0 elsewhere.

Max pooling, vectorized
Same network, one vector operation per window: still four hardmaxes
One vector rule per window: o = Σ a ⊙ x, with a = hardmax(x).

Hardmax → softmax pooling
Hardmax gets a gradient only to the winner. Can we soften the gate?
?
Softer gates, same problem. Can't see beyond the greater context.

Softmax pooling → attention
?
Softmax pooling across all four quadrants. The gate needs a score per quadrant. From what?
Key k = x WKᵀ: what each quadrant has. Query q = xTL WQᵀ: what top-left looks for. Score s = q · k
Two projections of the input, multiplied together. Where have we seen that before?
SwiGLU's pattern: projections feed the gate. Here s = (xTLWQᵀ) · (xjWKᵀ): how similar query and key are
Softmax pooling with one change: the gate reads projections, q · k, not raw values.
WV not drawn. The gates are plain numbers, so Σj aj(WVxj) = WV(Σj ajxj): WV can come after the gated sum and merge into the next linear layer. Running example: WV = I.

Before attention each quadrant knows only itself. Top-left is just blue: [1, 0, 0].
Attention output: a shadow boat everywhere, and all four quadrants are now identical. The boat quadrant lost what it was.
Fix: add each quadrant back, x + attention. This skip is a residual connection; it stays in the network from here on.
Top-left: [1, 0, 0] → [2, 0, 0.71]. It knows it is water, not just blue, because of the boat. No extra layer needed.
This breaks the CNN assumption that only local information matters.

Variance through attention
Assume every input x has variance σ². Follow it through the usual diagram.
?
QUESTION
x has variance σ². What variance should each weight have so the projection keeps σ²?
QUESTION
With that init, what is the variance of each element of Q, K, V?
QUESTION
What is the variance of each score after MatMul QKᵀ?
QUESTION
What comes out of the softmax as d grows?
QUESTION
σ⁴ = 1 when σ² = 1, but d keeps growing. How would you fix it?
ANSWER
Var(w) = 1/fan_in, std 1/√fan_in: LeCun (fan-in) init. Each output sums fan_in terms w·x.
ANSWER
Var(qi) = fan_in · (1/fan_in) · σ² = σ². Same for K and V.
ANSWER
d products of σ²·σ², added: Var(s) = d·σ⁴. σ⁴ is fine while σ² = 1; d is not.
ANSWER
High variance forces the gate to act like a hardmax: top gate → 1, the rest → 0.

BACK TO LECUN (FAN-IN) INIT
  • LeCun init fixed a sum of fan_in terms with 1/√fan_in
  • Same move here: divide the scores by √d
  • Var(s/√d) = σ⁴: 1 when σ² = 1, whatever d is
  • Toy model, d = 256: accuracy 1.00 with it, 0.51 without
softmax(QKᵀ/√d) V
LeCun init's move again: ÷√d keeps the scores' variance from growing with d.

Output projection
Merge the heads' channels back into one model-width map, so it can be added to the input.
WHAT IS FIXED
Q, K and V projections, and the output projection: learned weights, the same for every picture.
The output projection is a 1 × 1 conv across the stacked channels.
WHAT IS COMPUTED
The gates: softmax(QKᵀ/√d). They come from the picture, fresh every time.
A conv kernel is learned once. A head's mixing weights are built on the fly.

Rotary position encoding (RoPE)
Each pair of query or key numbers is an arrow: turn it by its position × θ
POSITIONS 2 AND 5
q at 2: turn 2θ → [0.54, 0.84]
k at 5: turn 5θ → [-0.80, 0.60]
q · k = 0.071
BOTH SHIFTED BY 3: 5 AND 8
q at 5: turn 5θ → [-0.80, 0.60]
k at 8: turn 8θ → [-0.65, -0.76]
q · k = 0.071
WHY
  • The score sees the angle between: (5 − 2)θ = (8 − 5)θ
  • Same offset, same score
  • Only Q and K turn
  • 2D: half the channels by column, half by row
NOW  A query and a key, before turning
© 2026 Dr. Jesse Roberts
RoPE in 2D
Split the query and key channels in half. One half turns by column, the other by row.
SCORE
q · k = column-offset term
+ row-offset term
A dot product is a sum over channels, so the two halves just add.
WHERE IT GOES
On queries and keys only. Never on values, never on the residual stream.
Which channels get which axis doesn't matter: the projections learn to fill them.
Caveat: no single pair turns with both row and column, so diagonals aren't direct. Later variants learn mixed directions.

© 2026 Dr. Jesse Roberts
A stalled parameter: how to spot it
Symptom: offset bias at default lr 0.58, no position at all 0.58. The bias adds nothing.
CHECK 1 · GRADIENT
Is the bias even learning?
CHECK 1 · GRADIENT
‖∇b‖ from 10−6 to 10−3: never zero. It is learning, just slowly.
CHECK 2 · REACH
How far can Adam move one entry in 630 steps?
CHECK 2 · REACH
Adam steps ≈ lr, whatever the gradient size (Quiz 3). Reach = Σ lrt = 0.63; measured max 0.49.
CHECK 3 · NEEDED SIZE
How big must a bias be to pick 1 patch of 100?
CHECK 3 · NEEDED SIZE
Score gap ≈ ln 100 ≈ 4.6. A bias of 0.49 gives only e0.49 ≈ 1.6× the odds.
FIXES
  • 10× lr for the bias group (reach 6.3) → 1.00
  • Train 3× longer (30 epochs) → 1.00
  • Or rescale the parameter: b = 10·b′
Adam([{"params": rest}, {"params": bias, "lr": 10*lr}])
If a parameter must grow big, check it can: Adam's reach ≈ lr × steps.
Reach is approximate (one Adam step briefly hit 3.7× lr). In practice: log max |w| and ‖Δw‖/‖w‖ per parameter group (diag_bias.py).

Why bother?
We built a lot of machinery to get back what a CNN already had
?
FAIR QUESTION
On the square-and-circle task, the CNN scores 1.00 too. So why replace it?
1Context at layer one. Every patch reads every patch in one step: sky or water, settled.
2Input-dependent mixing. Gates computed from each picture; a conv kernel is fixed.
3One shape for any sequence. Patches today, words next: same block.
4The catch: it needs data. Fewer built-in assumptions, more to learn.
Attention trades built-in assumptions for flexibility.

Class token as attention pooling
The CNN's last step, global average pooling, becomes attention too.
GLOBAL AVERAGE POOLING
weights: 1/N each
Attention where every gate is equal. Ignores content.
CLASS TOKEN
weights: softmax(q_cls Kᵀ/√d)
A learned query added as one extra token. It attends over every patch; its output goes to the linear head.
MODEL SO FAR
conv front end

The class token is attention pooling over the whole picture.

One deletion from the hybrid. Everything after it stays the same.
THE PATCH PROJECTION
  • Raw pixels → 16 × 16 patches
  • One shared projection:
conv, kernel 16 × 16, stride 16
  • No nonlinearity, no overlap
WHAT IS LOST
  • Stacked local filters
  • Even neighbours must be learned through attention
Pure ViT = hybrid minus the convolutions.

One long row of pixels, cut into 768-pixel windows; attention runs over the windows

QUESTION
ModernBERT (2024) went pre‑norm. Why?
Post-norm puts a LayerNorm on every skip path, so the gradient to early layers crosses them all; pre-norm keeps a clean skip path: deep stacks train stably.
Warner et al. 2024; Xiong et al. 2020
11WHY REUSE E AT THE OUTPUT?
Input gradient is sparse: a word's row learns only when it appears. The output softmax touches every row, every step. Tying gives every row that signal.
But the jobs differ (read vs. predict). Many large models untie (more data; dense signal not needed). Tying saves ≈23 M parameters here.
BERT = our model, on text, pretrained.
BERT-Base, Devlin et al. 2019: ≈ 110 M parameters. Pretrained on raw text: fill in hidden words (15%). Tying saves ≈ 23 M.

Takeaways
  • Attention: projections decide the gates and mixture based on context
  • Summation needed a variance correction again ÷√d
  • Heads ask several questions; concat × WO mixes them
  • Attention ignores position: add it back with a learned offset bias (RoPE in modern models)
  • ViT = patches + EncoderBlock (pre-norm, residual); BERT = same block on words, MLM
  • Cut anything into tokens: any modality joins in
  • Trains in parallel, unlike RNNs → foundation models
